Native primarily to the snowy boreal forests of the Russian Far East and parts of northeastern China, adult males can grow up to 10–12 feet in length and weigh over 600 pounds, while females are noticeably smaller. They are uniquely adapted to extreme cold, featuring a dense, pale orange coat with fewer and wider stripes, a thick layer of belly fat, and shaggy winter fur. As solitary apex predators, their diet consists mainly of wild boar, elk, and deer, and they can consume up to 60 pounds of meat in a single meal. Although their numbers dropped critically low in the 20th century due to poaching and habitat loss, dedicated conservation efforts have helped stabilize wild populations to roughly 500 to 600 individuals, keeping them listed as endangered. #tiger #tigeredit #tigercat #siberiantiger #amurtiger

This haunting footage was captured moments before the fatal tiger mauling in Yorkshire. Footage has emerged appearing to show a man in his 20s approaching a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park shortly before he was killed inside the enclosure on Saturday, October 10. The man can be seen filming himself near five-year-old Siberian tiger Altai as horrified visitors shout ‘Oh my God’ from the viewing platform above. Onlookers reportedly tried to stop him climbing over the barrier and entering the enclosure. The park remains closed following the tragedy, while it has been confirmed that Altai will not be euthanised.
